harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (Alpine 3.23, sudo 1.9.17p2) so every sudo command is recorded to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp, and no longer reaches the general system log. Previously sudo used its compiled-in default of logging via syslog's authpriv facility straight into /var/log/messages. Added /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-logging with `Defaults !syslog`, `Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"`, `Defaults log_year`, `Defaults log_host`, validated with visudo -c, and pre-created the log file (root:root, 600). Verified sudo commands now write entries like `Sep  4 23:08:02 2026 : root : HOST=node1 ; PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=...` to the dedicated file while /var/log/messages received no further sudo entries. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued a background `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnect, confirmed the node dropped and came back, proved boot_id changed (cbb5f7ee... -> 45013fd5..., uptime ~16s), and confirmed post-restart that the sudoers drop-in persisted, previously logged entries were retained, new sudo commands continued logging correctly to the dedicated file, and none leaked to /var/log/messages.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/sudo version and current sudo logging behavior (syslog authpriv -> /var/log/messages)
Created /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-logging with Defaults !syslog, logfile, log_year, log_host
Validated sudoers syntax with visudo -c
Pre-created /var/log/sudo-commands.log with root:root 600 permissions
Ran sudo commands and confirmed they logged to the dedicated file with user+timestamp and not to /var/log/messages
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime baseline on node1
Issued backgrounded reboot so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset, proving a real restart
Post-restart: re-validated sudoers config, confirmed prior log entries persisted, confirmed new sudo commands still route only to the dedicated log file

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands recorded to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
evidence.summary: Created and validated sudoers drop-in; log file shows entries like 'Sep 4 23:07:15 2026 : root : HOST=node1 ; PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=...'

evidence.requirement: Entries kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Baseline showed sudo previously wrote to /var/log/messages via syslog; after the change, /var/log/messages line count stayed flat while new sudo activity only appeared in sudo-commands.log
Captured boot_id cbb5f7ee-4877-4f2a-b797-79af01dff32e, uptime ~82s, sudoers drop-in content, log file permissions, and line counts before restart
Backgrounded reboot command returned REBOOT_ACK_SENT before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Exec failed with connection reset while node was down, then succeeded with new boot_id 45013fd5-e70e-4998-bfbf-014b540ad586 and uptime 15.99s, proving a genuine reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging config and data
evidence.summary: Sudoers drop-in intact and valid, prior 14 log lines preserved growing to 18 with new correctly formatted entries, and no corresponding entries appeared in /var/log/messages
